script:
## Hook
[ON SCREEN: "Chatbot" and "Agent" side by side, a question mark between them]
Your chatbot answers. Why can't it act?

## Relevance
[ON SCREEN: a student's project board with "Build an AI agent" pinned at the top]
If you are building AI projects, this difference decides what you actually build next.

## Example
[ON SCREEN: definition card - "What is a chatbot?", source: IBM]
A chatbot is a software application that communicates with people through text or voice. [C2]
[ON SCREEN: a chat bubble asking "When is my exam?" and a single reply]
Ask it when your exam is, and it answers, then waits for your next message.
[ON SCREEN: definition card - "What are AI agents?", source: IBM]
An agent is different: a system that autonomously performs tasks by designing workflows with available tools. [C3]
[ON SCREEN: illustrative flow, labelled "example": search, read, shortlist, calendar]
Give it a goal like "shortlist internships that match my résumé and add the deadlines to my calendar", and it plans the steps, searches, reads, shortlists and writes the entries itself.
[ON SCREEN: quote card, source: Anthropic, "Building effective agents"]
Anthropic describes agents as systems where the model directs its own process and tool use. [C1]

## Takeaway
[ON SCREEN: two-line checklist - "Only talks: chatbot" / "Pursues a goal, uses tools, acts: agent"]
So here is the test. If it only talks, it is a chatbot. If it pursues a goal and completes tasks for you, it is an agent. [C4]

## CTA
[ON SCREEN: Ziro logo and "ziro.digital"]
Explore AI learning at ziro.digital.

hooks.text: Before you build, know agent versus chatbot.
hooks.explanation: Warning formula: ties the distinction to the viewer's next project, which is why this audience cares; no open question, so less pull.

hooks.text: Your chatbot answers. Why can't it act?
hooks.explanation: Question formula: states what the viewer already knows (the chatbot answers), then opens the gap the video closes (why it can't act); says 'your' first, inside the 3-second hook window.

hooks.text: Stop calling your chatbot an AI agent.
hooks.explanation: Mistake formula: corrects a mix-up head-on; risks sounding preachy to beginners and promises a correction rather than a payoff.

hooks.text: Your chatbot answers. An agent acts.
hooks.explanation: The clearest six-word contrast, but it answers itself, so there is no gap left to close; best reused as the takeaway line.

hooks.text: Chatbot or agent: which one runs tasks?
hooks.explanation: Question formula framed as a choice; clear and on topic, but it names no stakes for the viewer, so it pulls less than a direct 'your' question.
